cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3). He opens by singing praises to the LORD about His loving devotion and His justice. Then David starts making promises, friend, and I mean promise after promise after PROMISE.
First, David says he'll ponder the way that is blameless. And right in the middle of that thought, he stops and asks the LORD a question.

cards.question: In the middle of his promise to ponder the blameless way, David asks the LORD why He has left him. True or false?

cards.text: Then David makes a big promise: he will walk with integrity of heart. And he names exactly where he's going to do it.

cards.question: Where does David say he'll walk with integrity of heart?

cards.text: Next, David makes a promise about his eyes: he'll set no worthless thing before them. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer staring at a takeout menu for a restaurant that closed, so I respect this man deeply.

cards.question: Then David talks about the work of those who fall away. What does he say about it?

answers.text: He hates it and it won't cling to him
He'll study it so he can learn from it
He'll leave it for someone else to judge

cards.text: Then David looks inward and says a perverse heart shall depart from him. Not "step out for a minute." DEPART.

cards.question: Along with a perverse heart departing, David says he will know nothing of ___.

cards.text: So far David's been talking about himself. Now he looks around at the people near him, and some of them are about to have a VERY awkward meeting.

cards.question: What does David say he'll do to whoever slanders a neighbor in secret?
David says he'll put up with someone who has haughty eyes and a proud heart, as long as they keep quiet. True or false?

cards.text: But David isn't only showing people the door. His eyes are out looking for someone, like a boss scrolling résumés with a VERY short list of what he's hiring for.

cards.question: Who do David's eyes favor, so they may dwell with him?

answers.text: The wise men of the east

cards.question: And the person who walks in the way of integrity? David says they'll get to ___ to him.

cards.text: Then David puts two kinds of people on the do-not-enter list for his house. No exceptions, no "but I know a guy."

cards.question: David says people who practice deceit can still dwell in his house, but people who tell lies can't stand in his presence. True or false?

cards.text: And David isn't saving this for someday. Like somebody who finally stops hitting the snooze button, he picks a time and sticks to it.

cards.question: When does David say he'll remove all the wicked of the land?
David says he'll cut off every evildoer from the city of the ___.

findings.problem: Card 2 only says David asks the LORD a question, and card 3 only rules out a made-up question. No card ever tells the baker what David actually asks: 'when will You come to me?' (Ps 101:2). The baker leaves Prep without one of the passage's key moments.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 2 says only that David asks the LORD a question. Nothing in it lets the baker reason whether the question is 'why He has left him', so the true/false pick is luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'David looks inward' treats the perverse heart in Ps 101:4 as David's own heart. The text says only 'A perverse heart shall depart from me' and leaves open whose heart it is. It could be a perverse person being sent away. Card 10's 'So far David's been talking about himself' builds on the same reading.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup says David puts two kinds of people on the do-not-enter list for his house. That already tells the baker that people who practice deceit can't dwell in his house, which rules out 'True' on card 17 before the baker answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card puts both kinds of people on the do-not-enter list 'for his house'. Ps 101:7 bars only those who practice deceit from dwelling in his house. Those who tell lies are barred from standing in his presence, which the text doesn't tie to the house.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The snooze button comparison points straight at morning, which gives away card 19's answer ('Every morning') and rules out 'Every new moon' and 'Every Sabbath'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
